title: Onboard nocturne-lite-6b v1.0 — perf metadata & changelog automation
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: Onboarding nocturne-lite-6b v1.0 into the model registry so it can be served by Redwood. This PR adds the canonical metadata JSON, curated performance profiles for common sequence lengths, unit/integration tests for registry validation, and hooks into the changelog/release-notes automation so model releases automatically surface in product-facing release notes. Motivation: nocturne-lite-6b is a cost-efficient 6B variant we want available for low-latency inference (esp. Dedicated and Private tiers). Changes include performance data derived from our perf-lab runs and a small automation script to populate the model changelog from registry metadata. What this PR does (high level): - Adds models/nocturne-lite-6b/metadata.json with schema-compliant fields (name, version, architecture, tokenizer, supported_apis, license, weights_uri, tags). - Adds models/nocturne-lite-6b/perf_profiles/*.json covering short/medium/long sequences with throughput/latency/kv-cache settings. - Adds tests: tests/model_registry/test_onboard_nocturne.py which validates schema and perf thresholds in CI. - Adds scripts/auto_changelog/generate_changelog.py: small utility used by the changelog workflow to convert metadata -> release note fragment. - Wires the model entry into the registry index and docs reference in docs/models.md. Checklist: - [x] metadata JSON conforms to registry schema (validated by local script) - [x] perf profiles produced from perf-lab runs (bench ids referenced in metadata) - [x] CI tests pass (unit + integration) - [x] changelog automation produces expected fragment (sample run included in PR comments) - [x] docs updated Notes on perf profiles: Profiles were produced from perf-canary run ids pf-2024-11-01-0830 and pf-2024-11-02-0215. We chose default_profile: "short" for low-latency API and provided conservative throughput numbers for Dedicated autoscaling guidance. See performance rationale in the metadata comments. If we observe regressions in production, the model can be disabled via the registry feature flag.
